findings.note: The sentence 'The statute does not mention hoarding.' is an absence-of-law claim. The ledger has no claim of type statute_absence for H&S 17920.3 (clm:1 to clm:8 are all affirmative statutes), so it is unproven (SR-6). Delete the sentence. The article can still avoid calling hoarded houses substandard by simply not saying it.

Who decides is stated as 'The local enforcement authority' (table row 1, last column) and 'The local enforcement authority makes that call' (paragraph after the table), plus 'not for you, me or a buyer to say'. No cited claim says that. The stored quote for clm:1 (17920.3(j)) names no decider at all, and the opening paragraph (clm:8) names none either. The statute's named deciders are in clm:2, clm:3 (health officer, or code enforcement officer if no agreement exists) and clm:4 (fire chief or deputy). Per SR-5, name those or say 'a local official, such as a health officer, a code enforcement officer or a fire chief'. For row 1, remove the claim that a specific authority decides, or reword to 'a local official, such as ...; confirm with your city or county'.
